author_read_locators.disposition: The theorem statement and source proof route were inspected. Appendix D.6 asserts that the conditional covariance equals the lower-right block of the inverse covariance and uses a Cmax-only eigenvalue bound; the matrix counterexample refutes that step. This source is not treated as a completed proof of either threshold branch. The upper implication is separately refuted by a constructed sequence.

sources.title: Martin J. Wainwright, Sharp Thresholds for High-Dimensional and Noisy Sparsity Recovery Using L1-Constrained Quadratic Programming (Lasso), IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 55 (2009), DOI 10.1109/TIT.2009.2016018

author_read_locators.locator: §IV.A, printed pp. 2190–2191, especially equations (28)–(35); proof §VI, printed pp. 2194–2195; Appendix I, printed p. 2200; Appendix K Lemmas 8–9, printed pp. 2200–2201.
author_read_locators.disposition: For a positive-definite symmetric matrix A, the revised paper defines rho_ell(A)=1/2 min_{i != j}(A_ii + A_jj - 2 A_ij), a minimum pairwise increment variance of the conditional covariance, not its least eigenvalue. Its lower threshold theta_ell(Sigma)=rho_ell(Sigma_{S^c|S})/[C_max(2-gamma(Sigma))^2] is a distinct interface; Appendix K gives Gaussian matrix spectral-norm bounds. These are source-reconciliation evidence, and no theorem is imported without a local complete proof.
